provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and scoring calibration pending.

title: Principal Engineer: Set a Migration Strategy Across Teams
prompt: Three product teams use a shared event interface. A proposed replacement improves versioning, but migration would consume 18 engineer-weeks this quarter. The available cross-team change capacity is 10 engineer-weeks. The draft strategy says, "Require every team to migrate by quarter-end; the platform team will handle any compatibility issues." You are a principal individual contributor with technical influence, not the teams’ line manager. Review the proposal and present a technical decision to the engineering director (the AI).

rubric.label: Identify the contract risk
rubric.description: Uses the actual shared-interface ambiguity to shape migration evidence.

anchors.0: Mandates migration by preference or claims the new interface necessarily fixes ordering.
anchors.2: Identifies timestamp semantics and seeks consumer evidence.
anchors.4: Defines the ambiguous contract and compatibility tests across producer/consumer versions, separates observed risk from unsupported incident claims and identifies evidence that would change the design choice.

rubric.label: Design a feasible transition
rubric.description: Compares transition options within real capacity.

anchors.0: Commits 18 engineer-weeks within 10 engineer-weeks or assumes an unowned layer is free.
anchors.2: Proposes staged migration or a compatibility layer.
anchors.4: Compares a bounded path migration and compatibility option against the 10-engineer-week constraint, includes verification and ownership, and sets explicit expansion/removal or rollback criteria without double-counting capacity.

rubric.label: Lead through influence and ownership
rubric.description: Clarifies cross-team adoption without inventing managerial authority.

anchors.0: Orders other teams to reprioritize unilaterally or leaves all compatibility to the platform team.
anchors.2: Consults managers and names technical owners.
anchors.4: Builds an evidence-backed decision record with accountable producer/consumer owners, negotiates capacity through managers/director and separates interface governance from line-management decisions.

reference.scenario: Three product teams use a shared event interface. A proposed replacement improves versioning, but migration would consume 18 engineer-weeks this quarter. The available cross-team change capacity is 10 engineer-weeks. The draft strategy says, "Require every team to migrate by quarter-end; the platform team will handle any compatibility issues." You are a principal individual contributor with technical influence, not the teams’ line manager. Review the proposal and present a technical decision to the engineering director (the AI).

facts.value: The shared interface has two incompatible interpretations of a timestamp field. There are no reported data-loss incidents, but consumers disagree about ordering. One team could migrate a low-volume path using two engineer-weeks of work. These are effort estimates; calendar duration depends on staffing and sequencing.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about the specific compatibility risk or a bounded pilot

facts.value: A compatibility layer requiring six engineer-weeks of work could support old and new consumers temporarily, but ongoing ownership and removal criteria are not assigned. Team managers control their engineers’ commitments.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about transition options, capacity or decision rights

model_points: Defines the ambiguous contract and compatibility tests across producer/consumer versions, separates observed risk from unsupported incident claims and identifies evidence that would change the design choice.

Compares a bounded path migration and compatibility option against the 10-engineer-week constraint, includes verification and ownership, and sets explicit expansion/removal or rollback criteria without double-counting capacity.
Builds an evidence-backed decision record with accountable producer/consumer owners, negotiates capacity through managers/director and separates interface governance from line-management decisions.

probes.question: Who can commit the other teams’ capacity?
What prevents it becoming an indefinite second interface?
Which contract tests and migration decisions must change?

fair_alternatives: Keeping the current interface while clarifying semantics can be valid if the risk and maintenance cost are compared.
A phased direct migration can be valid without a compatibility layer when consumer sequencing is supported.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess only the decisions and reasoning demonstrated in this fictional exercise. No hiring-readiness, personality, legal compliance or workplace performance claim follows from this score. A valid alternative can earn full credit. Unrevealed conditional facts must not be assumed known or required for credit; credit asking for needed information and a conditional plan.

interviewer_notes: You are the counterpart named in the prompt. If this is a written review, remain the hiring interviewer while the candidate reads and writes. Let the candidate finish, including thinking and self-correction. Answer only supplied facts when their reveal condition is met; otherwise say the information is unknown. Use neutral probes after a completed answer, one at a time. Do not prescribe the rubric as a spoken checklist. Accept relevant examples from work, education and community leadership. Do not request private employee records, infer protected traits, invent employment rules or promise a real organizational outcome. Simulation gives no answer before assessment; coaching may offer labeled assistance.

learning_drills.title: Write a cross-team technical decision
learning_drills.prompt: Write the contract problem, competing options, a capacity-feasible first step and evidence for expanding or reversing it. This is self-guided practice with no automated assessment.
checklist: Use influence rather than assumed line authority
